findings: Both dated method pages describe the Japan-origin wallet, JPY, same 50–1,000,000 JPY limits, standard payout scheduling and unavailable recurring, Connect, disputes and manual capture. November explicitly limits payment acceptance to domestic JP commerce and single use, with no Setup Intents, setup_future_usage or off-session. The API and UI product-matrix distinctions retain Payment Links, Checkout and Payment Element while specifying full-page, embedded and in-app support and no Express Checkout Element, Terminal or Billing. Radar requires private-preview access.

JP merchant B2B/B2C applicants can have instant provisional activation and post-activation review. The site needs matching onboarding information, identified products/services and payment flow, digital offerings disclosure where relevant and complete SCTA page. It prohibits MCC 6051 and permits an appeal for restrictions.

Customer chooses PayPay, opens it via desktop QR/web or mobile app/browser, authorizes separately with PayPay and can return automatically or manually. Stripe immediately confirms success or failure. Standard redirect differs from the eligible custom QR variant that keeps the page open; the two expiration clocks have different triggers and actors.

Merchant full or partial refunds submitted through Dashboard/API within 365 days complete instantly, cannot be canceled, and are handled by PayPay back to the original PayPay balance or linked funding source without reversal. Stripe's Refund status and webhook types are separate; failed refund restores merchant Stripe balance and needs another refund method. PayPay can send customer dispute inquiries to merchant for a refund, with no standard chargeback or dispute debit.
Stripe passes a computed descriptor to the PayPay partner integration, which controls display. The linked Connect descriptor guidance does not imply PayPay Connect eligibility.

The PayPay method profiles exclude Connect.
